summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Mendota Health through the Model Catalog UI and API. Focus was on selecting open models for clinical summarization and triage, understanding benchmark numbers (latency, tokens/sec, cost estimates), and verifying compatibility with Mendota's on-prem GPU fleet and VPC requirements. Action: provide compatibility matrix, benchmarks spreadsheet, and pilot SOW; schedule infra deep dive.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood. We'll do a quick intros, then Priya will walk through the model catalog demo and API examples.
[00:12] Alicia Gomez: Hi, Alicia here at Mendota, CTO. We've got Mark and Sam as well. We're mostly interested in using open models for clinical note summarization, and also cost/latency tradeoffs.
[00:25] Mark Rivers: Yes, hi. We're sensitive about PHI, so private deployment is a hard requirement long term. For a pilot we can use Dedicated or a VPC.
[00:35] Priya Shah: Great, thanks. I'll share my screen if anyone can't see let me know. So first slide is the model catalog it's a curated list of open models, vendor-verified perf profiles, and compatibility notes.
[00:50] Priya Shah: (screen) You'll see filters: architecture, seq length, task tags, quantization support. For example, LLama2 variants, Mistral, and some trimmed clinical-tuned models.
[01:10] Sam Patel: Quick question how accurate are the perf numbers? Our infra is mixed A100 and some older T4s, we care about tail latency for single-request inference.
[01:22] Priya Shah: Good Q. Benchmarks are collected with our internal harness; we show avg token latency, p95, and throughput at different batch sizes. We also publish a compatibility matrix: which quant levels (4-bit, 8-bit), supported kernels, and recommended GPU. It's in the catalogue and as a spreadsheet. Link: https://redwood.example/benchmarks/mendota-demo.xlsx
[01:45] Mark Rivers: Are those numbers from hosted or on-prem runs? Because kernel selection differs.
[01:50] Priya Shah: Most are from our hosted infra across common hardware, but we include notes for on-prem differences and a per-model kernel fallback. For an on-prem pilot we recommend running our lightweight benchmark agent against your GPU fleet to get exact p95s.
[02:10] Jordan Lee: To frame selection for summarization we've seen a nice tradeoff using the 'mistral-clinical-7b' quantized to 4-bit for cost-sensitive infra, and a larger 13b variant for higher fidelity where latency can tolerate it.
[02:25] Alicia Gomez: We have a lot of short notes, 150-400 tokens each, so seq length isn't huge. Latency per single request matters more than throughput.
[02:35] Priya Shah: Perfect. In catalog you can sort by p95 for single-token generation or by tokens/sec for batching. There's also a routing policy block if a model is unavailable we automatically fallback to a compatible variant with a flag for quality degrade.
[02:55] Sam Patel: What's the fallback behaviour for KV cache? We need consistent session state for multi-turn summaries.
[03:05] Priya Shah: We persist KV cache per session; fallback to a variant keeps the cache mapping; there can be small tokenization differences which we flag as potential drift. (murmur) Sorry, sometimes transcript picks up KV as 'K V cash' in older exports.
[03:25] Mark Rivers: On the compatibility matrix, does Redwood list which models support Triton or other runtime kernels?
[03:30] Priya Shah: Yes columns include supported runtimes (Torch, Triton, TensorRT), recommended kernel, quantization tested (q4_0, q4_1, q8), and example docker images.
[03:48] Jordan Lee: I'll jump in with the API demo quick cURL example for model selection: POST /v1/generate with model: 'mistral-clinical-7b-q4' and optional route_hint: 'low_latency'. You can also pin model versions for rollouts.
[04:05] Alicia Gomez: Can we run a canary that routes 10% to hosted and 90% to Dedicated? We want gradual rollout without user-facing interruption.
[04:12] Priya Shah: Absolutely sorry (encoding glitch) Console supports canaries and A/B, and automatic fallback policies if Dedicated capacity is exceeded. You set a policy like: prefer dedicated, fallback to hosted, max latency 300ms.
[04:30] Sam Patel: What about encryption at rest and KMS? We need HSM integration for keys.
[04:35] Jordan Lee: Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM and customer-managed keys. We'll include our security docs and SOC2 artifact. I'll share those after the call.
[04:50] Mark Rivers: Objection our procurement team will push back on sustained cost. Can you show cost estimates?
[04:55] Priya Shah: In the catalog we show relative cost per 1k tokens for each model and an estimated monthly cost calculator based on reqs per minute. We can run your workload trace to produce an exact estimate.
[05:12] Priya Shah: (navigates) Here's a benchmark chart p95 latency vs cost per 1k tokens. See how the 7b quantized curve gives low cost with decent latency; 13b increases cost but improves ROUGE/accuracy metrics per our evals.
[05:35] Alicia Gomez: Those evals are they clinical-specific or general? We need to know if hallucination risk is measured on our clinical prompts.
[05:42] Priya Shah: Good point catalog has both general evals and domain evals when available. For clinical we recommend a small eval harness you run with a labeled prompt set; Redwood offers to run it as part of the pilot.
[05:58] Mark Rivers: We also need the compatibility matrix for our on-prem multi-tenant cluster. Can Redwood guarantee isolation with Dedicated vs Private?
[06:06] Jordan Lee: Yes Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and tenant isolation; Private is full VPC/on-prem where you control network and data residency. We'll note the differences in the doc we send.
[06:20] Sam Patel: Practical question what's the effort to deploy the benchmark agent on-prem? We have strict change windows.
[06:25] Priya Shah: The agent is a lightweight container; typical install is one hour, it runs offline and only reports metrics to your control plane if you permit. We'll coordinate with your SRE.
[06:40] (pause, typing)
[07:00] Priya Shah: Live API demo now generating a summary with mistral-clinical-7b-q4, showing streaming tokens, and how you can instrument token cost hooks in the SDK.
[07:20] Mark Rivers: The streaming looks good. For audit logs we need token-level traces tied to session IDs do you expose that in the console?
[07:27] Jordan Lee: Yes, the Console has per-request logs, token counts, latencies, and a tracing hook you can push to our observability pipeline or export to your SIEM.
[07:40] Alicia Gomez: One more compliance question data retention defaults and ability to disable retention on Hosted.
[07:45] Jordan Lee: You can set retention policies per customer; for Private you control retention. For Hosted we have configurable retention windows and options to disable storage of user payloads. We'll include the data retention matrix.
[07:58] Priya Shah: Back to model selection here's a compatibility snippet for inference config you can paste into our CLI. Example: model: mistral-clinical-7b-q4, runtime: triton, num_gpus: 1, max_batch: 4.
[08:15] Sam Patel: Does Redwood support elastic batching across multiple GPU types? Our cluster mixes A100 and A10G.
[08:22] Priya Shah: We do workload-aware batching and can route by GPU capability; if a request requires a kernel only supported on A100 we'll route accordingly but define cost and latency tradeoffs.
[08:35] Mark Rivers: Can we tag models as 'approved for PHI' after our QA? We need RBAC on who can deploy which model.
[08:42] Jordan Lee: Console supports model-level RBAC and approvals workflow. We'll demo that in a follow-up demo with your security team.
[08:55] (crosstalk)
[09:05] Priya Shah: Okay, wrapping up I'll send the compatibility matrix and the benchmarks spreadsheet; Jordan will send pricing and the pilot SOW. Proposed pilot: 4-week dedicated pilot using your on-prem A100s, run our benchmark agent, run evals on a sample of 5k clinical notes, then decide roll to Private.
[09:25] Alicia Gomez: Sounds good. Timeline sounds reasonable. Procurement will need the SOW and security pack.
[09:32] Jordan Lee: Noted. Any other Qs?
[09:40] Mark Rivers: One quick technical: tokenization differences across model variants do you normalize tokens before comparing results?
[09:45] Priya Shah: We include tokenizer mapping notes and recommend canonicalization in the eval harness; we can share our tokenizer scripts.
[09:59] Sam Patel: I'll upload our GPU inventory and a sample inference trace to the shared folder after the call.
[10:05] Jordan Lee: Great, thanks Sam. We'll follow up with the docs.
[10:12] Alicia Gomez: Thanks everyone, appreciate the demo.
[10:18] Jordan Lee: Thanks, talk soon.
